name: Amagi Media Labs Ltd
title: Amagi Media Labs Ltd - 544679 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Non-financial AI-in-media webinar with no company numbers, guidance or capex; management explicitly declined company-specific questions, so no supply-side or pricing read is available.

evasions.topic: Company performance, SLAs and cost savings evidence
evasions.quote: I wouldn't want to talk about the business
This is not the forum for it. We'll probably take it up at a later point.

summary.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
summary.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

risks_watch: Hallucination and unpredictability of agentic AI against strict uptime SLAs, which management said it addresses with guardrails but gave no metrics for.
Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.
Possible shift in vendor pricing toward outcome-based models, which would change revenue recognition, though management said it is not yet visible.
The webinar did not address Amagi's own Q1 FY27 numbers, so the company's operating and financial trajectory remains unassessed; the company directed investors to ir@amagi.com for follow-up.
summary.management_tone: Management was enthusiastic and expansive on long-term AI themes, but deliberately avoided Amagi-specific answers, redirecting company questions to generic industry views. Cautious on near-term monetisation, describing most AI use as early and expansionary rather than cost-saving.
key_quotes: So, a lot of work that our company, and I'm sure lots of companies are doing, is to bring determinism to an indeterministic problem.
for every dollar that they've been spending on technology, there's $2 to $4 of human toil.
Most of our customers are looking at more of an expansionary aspect, not as a cost saving capability as it stands today.

growth.why: The 7 July 2026 AI-in-media webinar explicitly excluded financials, outlook and operational metrics, so there is no guided growth, capacity addition or quarterly result to record.
